title: Three letters, then a Book that is clear.
subtitle: A pause before a plain message
then: This surah came in Makkah after years of the Prophet ﷺ calling his people, while their mockery only grew. It opens with three letters whose meaning is known to Allah. Then it says what follows is {idea}a Book, and a clear Quran{/idea}.
now: You open the app between two notifications, thumb already itching to scroll. The letters at the start do not explain themselves. They just make you stop. {idea}The message after them is plain enough to act on.{/idea}
old: I need to understand everything before the Quran can speak to me.
new: Some things are Allah's to know; what He made clear is mine to take.
try: Before reading your next passage, sit still for ten seconds with the phone face down.

title: A day comes when they wish they had submitted.
subtitle: Regret that arrives too late

row.title: the wish
sub: if only we had been Muslims

then: Ibn Kathir explains that those who rejected faith will one day {trap}regret having lived in disbelief{/trap}. Some early scholars said this wish comes when they see believers who sinned being brought out of Hell by Allah's mercy.
now: You know the feeling after a missed call from someone who is now gone. You meant to call back. The verse points at a bigger version of that. {idea}The time to turn is while the line is still open.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about my faith once life calms down.
new: The regret the verse describes is avoidable, but only from this side.
try: Do one act of worship today you have been saving for later.

title: Eating, enjoying, and distracted by hope.
subtitle: When long plans push out repentance

picture.label: A full life, missing one thing

then: Allah tells His Messenger ﷺ to leave the mockers to their meals and pleasures. Ibn Kathir calls it a stern threat. Their {trap}long hopes distracted them from repentance{/trap} and from turning to Allah, until they would come to know.
now: The five-year plan on your notes app. The holiday you are saving for. The promotion. None of it is wrong. {trap}But it can fill every hour{/trap} until there is no room left to ask if you are right with Allah.
old: I have plenty of time; there are other things to sort out first.
new: Hopes for this life are fine until they crowd out turning back to Allah.
try: Add one line to tomorrow's to-do list: a minute of seeking forgiveness.

title: Every town that fell had a known decree.
subtitle: Nothing ends by accident
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah never destroys a town until {idea}He has given it clear evidence{/idea} and its time has run out. This was a warning to the people of Makkah to leave their stubbornness while they still could.
now: You notice the doctor's warnings, the friend who keeps saying something is off, the small signs at work. Warnings come before endings. {idea}Hearing them is a mercy, not a nuisance.{/idea}
old: Bad endings just happen out of nowhere.
new: Allah sends signs first; the end comes only after the term is written and met.
try: Think of one warning someone gave you recently. Take it seriously for a day.

title: No nation moves its deadline, early or late.
subtitle: The term is fixed
then: Right after saying every town has a known decree, the verse adds that {idea}no nation can bring its term forward or push it back{/idea}. Ibn Kathir reads it as a plain warning to Makkah: the time is set, so change now.
now: The hospital corridor, waiting for news you cannot speed up. Or a deadline at work you wish would move. Some times are simply not in your hands. {reward}What you do before them is.{/reward}
old: If I worry enough, I can somehow control how long things last.
new: The time is Allah's; the deeds inside it are mine.
try: Let go of one worry about timing today and spend that energy on one good deed.

title: They called the bearer of the Reminder mad.
subtitle: Mockery used instead of an answer
then: The Quraysh mocked the Prophet ﷺ as {trap}one who only claims to receive the Reminder{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says they called him mad because he invited them to leave the way of their forefathers.
now: In the family group chat, someone shares a reminder about prayer and gets an eye-roll emoji. You have done it too, maybe. {idea}Mocking the messenger is easier than facing the message.{/idea}
old: If someone sounds strange, I can dismiss what they say.
new: An insult is often how people avoid a truth that asks them to change.
try: The next time a reminder annoys you, ask what part of it is true before reacting.

title: Bring us angels, they demanded, if you are honest.
subtitle: Setting conditions for believing
then: After calling him mad, they asked why he did not {trap}bring angels to bear witness{/trap} for him. Ibn Kathir compares it to Pharaoh asking why angels were not sent along with Musa.
now: You tell yourself you will start praying once you feel something. Once you get a sign. Once life proves it. {trap}You are writing the terms for Allah.{/trap} The signs around you are already speaking.
old: I will commit when I get the proof I want.
new: Asking for my own kind of proof can be a way of saying no politely.
try: Write down one sign of Allah's care you already received this week.

title: When angels descend, the waiting is over.
subtitle: Why their demand was dangerous

row.title: the end of time to repent

then: Allah answers the demand. Angels are sent down only {idea}with the truth{/idea}, which Mujahid explained as the message and the punishment. If they came as asked, {trap}the deniers would get no more respite{/trap}.
now: You keep waiting for one big moment to force you to change. But when the truly big moment comes, there is no after. {reward}The quiet time you have now is the gift.{/reward}
old: A dramatic sign would make it easier for me to change.
new: The quiet time before the final sign is mercy, not a lack of proof.
try: Change one small thing today without waiting for a push.

title: Allah sent the Reminder and Allah guards it.
subtitle: The Quran is protected by its Sender
then: They mocked the Prophet ﷺ as one who only claimed to receive the Reminder. Allah replies that {idea}it is He who sent it down{/idea}, and Ibn Kathir notes He {reward}protects it from being changed or altered{/reward}.
now: You hear a clip online claiming the Quran was rewritten, or you feel your own faith wobbling. The Book in your hand is not held up by you. {reward}Allah keeps it.{/reward} Your part is to read it.
old: I have to defend the Quran or it might be lost.
new: Allah guards His Book; my job is to live by it.
try: Read one page of the Quran today, slowly, as a message kept just for you.

title: You are not the first messenger sent.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ

key.label: How it feels vs. what is true

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah was {idea}consoling His Messenger ﷺ{/idea} after Quraysh rejected him. The surah introduction notes he had grown tired after years of effort. Allah reminds him that messengers came before him to earlier peoples.
now: You are the only one in the office who prays. Or the only one at home trying to keep the family calm. {idea}Others walked this before you{/idea}, and Allah saw each of them.
old: Nobody has ever been in a spot as lonely as mine.
new: I am walking a path many before me walked, and they were not left alone.
try: Read a short story of one earlier prophet tonight and notice what he faced.

title: Every messenger who came was mocked.
subtitle: Ridicule is an old pattern
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}no messenger came to a nation without being rejected and mocked{/trap}. For the Prophet ﷺ, facing ridicule in Makkah, this meant the laughter was not a sign he had failed.
now: You start wearing hijab, or you stop drinking at work dinners, and someone jokes about it. It stings. {idea}The joke says more about an old pattern than about you.{/idea}
old: If people laugh at what I do, I must be doing it wrong.
new: Being mocked for doing right has happened to the best people who ever lived.
try: Next time a joke stings, answer it with calm kindness, then let it go.

title: Stubborn hearts let denial settle in.
subtitle: What arrogance does to the heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah lets disbelief enter the hearts of those {trap}too stubborn and too arrogant{/trap} to follow His guidance. Anas and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said what enters is shirk.
now: Someone corrects you in a meeting and you are right that they are wrong, so you dig in. Next time you dig in faster. {trap}Pride makes the next refusal easier.{/trap} The heart hardens one stubborn moment at a time.
old: My heart just drifts on its own; I am not responsible for it.
new: Each time I refuse out of pride, I make room for the next refusal.
try: Today, accept one correction without defending yourself.

title: They will not believe, though history already spoke.
subtitle: The way of earlier peoples is known
then: The stubborn would not believe in the Quran. Yet Ibn Kathir says {idea}the way of the earlier peoples was well known{/idea}: Allah destroyed those who rejected His messengers and {reward}saved the prophets and their followers{/reward}.
now: You have watched a friend ignore every warning about a habit and lose a lot to it. You know how that story goes. {idea}The question is whether you read your own life with the same eyes.{/idea}
old: What happened to people long ago does not tell me anything.
new: The past is a map of how rejection and faith usually end.
try: Pick one lesson from someone else's mistake and apply it to yourself this week.

title: Even a gate into the sky would not convince them.
subtitle: When the problem is not lack of proof
then: They had demanded angels. Allah says that even if a {idea}gate to heaven were opened{/idea} and they climbed through it, they would still refuse. Ibn Kathir calls it the extent of their {trap}stubborn resistance to the truth{/trap}.
now: You ask a friend for advice, then argue with every answer. Ten more answers would not help. {trap}You had already decided.{/trap} Sometimes the problem is not the evidence. It is the will.
old: If I just had more evidence, I would change.
new: When my heart refuses, no amount of proof is enough.
try: Name one thing you keep asking about but already know the answer to. Act on it.

title: Our eyes were tricked, they would say.
subtitle: Explaining away what you clearly saw

key.label: Two ways to meet a sign

then: Even after climbing into heaven, they would say {trap}our eyes have been dazzled, we are bewitched{/trap}. Ibn Zayd said the dazzled one is like someone intoxicated, who cannot reason.
now: Your prayer is answered and you call it coincidence. You recover and say it was just the medicine. {trap}There is always an explanation ready.{/trap} The verse asks you to notice the habit of explaining Allah away.
old: There is a normal explanation for everything good that happens to me.
new: The habit of explaining away signs can blind me as much as any spell.
try: Tonight, name one good thing from today and thank Allah for it by name.
